title: Reverse WAL group-commit window: commit_delay 100->0, commit_siblings 2->5
configuration_cause: The accepted r003 bundle opened a 100us commit_delay group-commit window with commit_siblings=2 while only ~5 terminals commit; the window adds per-commit stall without collecting enough siblings, and wal_writer_flush_after=0 removed the writer's flush batching. The mechanism verdict was refuted: sync_average_ms did not fall consistently (6.5% then -5.2%) and wal_bytes_per_txn rose 15-19%.
mechanism: r003's WAL commit-path bundle was accepted on Goodput but its stated mechanism (fewer/cheaper WAL syncs) was refuted: sync_average_ms was inconsistent and wal_bytes_per_txn rose. With only 5 terminals and commit_siblings=2, commit_delay=100us mostly adds a fixed stall to each commit rather than batching siblings, and wal_writer_flush_after=0 disables the background writer's flush batching. Reversing the group-commit window (commit_delay->0, commit_siblings->5) and restoring a modest writer flush batch (wal_writer_flush_after 0->64) removes the added commit stall while keeping the accepted WAL buffer capacity and compression. This tests whether the Goodput gain came from buffering/compression rather than the delay window.
query_effect: InsertTweet commits no longer pay a fixed 100us group-commit stall; GetUserTweets read path unchanged.
expected_tps_effect: Small increase or neutral; removes per-commit stall while retaining accepted WAL buffering and compression.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 should fall modestly; overall p95 neutral.

predictions.rationale: Removing the commit_delay window and restoring writer flush batching should reduce average sync latency versus the 0.1305ms incumbent.
Removing the fixed 100us commit stall lowers InsertTweet tail latency.
Freed commit-path stall should raise completed transaction Goodput.

alternatives.statement: If the Goodput gain came entirely from wal_buffers/compression, reversing commit_delay will be neutral on sync_average_ms and TPS.
If the group-commit window genuinely batched siblings, removing it will increase sync_average_ms and lower TPS.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Removes a per-commit stall that the refuted mechanism shows was not buying sync batching at 5 terminals, while preserving the accepted WAL buffer capacity and compression that plausibly drove the Goodput gain.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Reverse the 0->100 window; 0 is the safe low bound, removing the fixed per-commit stall.
Restore activation threshold to 5, matching ~5 terminals so group commit only triggers when real siblings exist; within safe [0,20].
Restore a modest 64*8kB flush batch (safe [0,1024]) so the WAL writer batches flushes instead of flushing every write.

nodes.label: Reverse WAL group-commit window: commit_delay 0, commit_siblings 5, wal_writer_flush_after 64
Remove fixed per-commit stall; restore writer flush batching while keeping WAL buffers/compression

cross_domain_requirements: Do not re-enable commit_delay>0 without evidence of >10 concurrent committing terminals
